newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli U.S. equity offerings to surge - Prudential.
newsitem.headline: Israeli U.S. equity offerings to surge - Prudential.

text.p: The number of Israeli companies making initial public offerings (IPOs) on U.S. equity markets could rise by 40 percent this year compared with 1996, a Prudential Securities executive forecast on Tuesday.

Israel, with 75 firms listed in the United States, is second only to Canada as the foreign country with the most companies traded in the United States. Last year, 18 Israeli firms made IPOs on U.S. markets against six in 1995.
"I think it could be up 40 percent," Paul Scura, head of investment banking at Prudential in New York, told reporters when asked about prospects for Israeli IPOs this year in the United States.
Prudential was a co-sponsor of a Tel Aviv symposium for Israeli companies on going public in the United States. It was the first time Prudential has held such an event abroad.

David Weild, another Prudential executive, said U.S. markets fuelled by investments from "baby boomers" now in the "saving phase of their life cycle" should continue to remain attractive to Israeli firms.

"Given that many of the technology companies...in Israel, have yet to really mature we would expect that the trend to go public in the United States should sustain itself...for the foreseeable future," Weild said.
"This has been a little bit like Silicon Valley East for us," he said.

While the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange slumped last year, Israeli companies raised $629 million through IPOs in the United States in 1996, a 16 percent increase over the previous year, according to figures by Ernst & Young, another co-sponsor of the seminar.

Yitzhak Forer, managing partner of Ernst & Young in Israel, noted that although high-tech firms had led the Israeli rush to Wall Street, Israeli industrial and service companies such as Koor Industries and Blue Square Israel had also begun making offerings in New York since 1995.
